patch_resolves_note: The fixed OpenThread build keeps the original 253-byte server-data case clean by checking the derived length before the server-data memcpy. The adjacent 248-byte boundary case still reaches the protected memcpy on both sides, giving a genuine fixed-side witness that the repaired path permits in-bounds copies.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

nodes.description: The first project parser step on the vulnerable path tokenizes the attacker-controlled UART command line in place, materializing the command and data arguments that later feed `ProcessService`.

The vulnerable code derives the server-data copy length from attacker-controlled `argv[3]` and reaches the following `memcpy` without any check that the length fits `cfg.mServerConfig.mServerData`. The fix adds the missing obligation with `length = strlen(argv[3]); VerifyOrExit(length <= sizeof(cfg.mServerConfig.mServerData), error = OT_ERROR_NO_BUFS);` before copying.

ASan sink. The reproduced run reaches the server-data copy with length 253 and writes 5 bytes past the 248-byte `cfg.mServerConfig.mServerData` array in stack local `cfg`, matching the `stack-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 253` report at `cli.cpp:1642`.

edges.description: The same derived server-data length produced at the missing-bound site is the length argument consumed by the immediately following memcpy sink.
edges.evidence: The vulnerable original trace records server_data_bound_check.server_data_length == server_data_copy.server_data_length == 253.
